title: Let trucks and the night close wait at the loading dock

blocks.text: A warehouse has a loading dock with a few bays. Trucks that arrive when every bay is taken wait for one to free up, and at night the yard manager's app waits for the dock to empty before it locks the gate. The dock's software has had three bad weeks: once the yard counted four trucks in three bays, a driver sat in front of a free bay for an hour, and the gate was locked with a truck still inside.

`LoadingDock` already keeps the count of occupied bays under its lock and has two conditions, `bayFree` and `dockEmpty`. Write its three small helpers in `src/main/java/practice/LoadingDock.java`; each is called with the lock held:

items: `waitForBay()`: returns once the arriving truck can take a bay;
`announceLeave()`: runs after a truck has left;
`waitForEmpty()`: returns once no truck is at the dock.

blocks.text: A truck never takes a bay that isn't free, a waiting truck gets in as soon as a bay frees, and the night close goes ahead only once the dock is empty, and then without delay. About four lines in total.

The tests run waiting trucks and the night close on threads of their own. To check that your waits hold up, they also take the dock's lock themselves: once to let a newcomer drive into a bay right after it was freed, and once to wake the night close while a truck is still in.

cases.says: trucks take free bays without waiting, and the night close of an empty dock returns at once
a waiting truck that is woken but finds the bay taken by a newcomer goes on waiting, so the dock never holds more trucks than bays
a truck waiting for a bay gets in when another truck leaves
the night close, waiting for the dock to empty, goes ahead when the last truck leaves
the night close, woken while a truck is still at the dock, goes on waiting

origin.section: A Condition Gives Up the Lock While It Waits, So Check Again After await()

concepts: A woken thread can find the state changed by another thread, or wake spuriously, so await() is called in a while loop over its condition.
Each change signals the condition the side that can now proceed waits on; signalling the wrong one leaves the waiter parked, and one shared condition needs signalAll().
